messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: People with MS who supplemented with vitamin D had significantly reduced depression risk (PHQ-2 positive screen).
Sentence: "Participants who supplemented with omega 3s, particularly flaxseed oil, had frequent fish consumption, supplemented with vitamin D, meditated, and had moderate alcohol consumption had significantly reduced depression risk."
Measured as: depression risk (PHQ-2 score ≥3)
Population: People with multiple sclerosis recruited internationally via Web 2.0 platforms
Intervention: Self-reported vitamin D supplementation
Comparator: Participants not supplementing with vitamin D
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 2,459
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study B tests vitamin C supplementation, not vitamin D, so it does not bear on the vitamin D question.","verdict":"off_question","reason":null,"also_differs":[],"detail":"exposure: vitamin C (500 mg twice daily), not vitamin D"}
